subject: Human Body
title: T Cells: Killers and Helpers
description: One-minute skill: T Cells: Killers and Helpers.

hook.text: T cells mature in the thymus, a gland behind your breastbone. They're trained there to ignore your own cells.

buildup.text: Helper T cells coordinate the response. They activate B cells, boost macrophages, and recruit more fighters.

discovery.text: Killer T cells destroy infected cells directly.

twist.text: HIV attacks helper T cells specifically. Without them, the entire immune system collapses — that's what causes AIDS.

climax.text: T cells are the generals and assassins. Helpers command the army. Killers execute infected cells one by one.

punchline.text: Helpers give orders. Killers carry them out. Both are T cells.

quiz.question: What does HIV target that collapses the immune system?
